# Story 03 — Roles & Permissions

## Prerequisites

- Story 01 completed: Authentication & Login (JWT issuance, `AuthController`, `JwtTokenService`, `ClaimsPrincipalExtensions`, seeded administrator).
- Story 02 completed: Users Management (`User` entity, `UsersController`, EF Core migrations pipeline).
- Coordination with owners of shared contracts: no other feature currently depends on the auth claim shape; extending it here is safe but must remain backward compatible with the existing token payload so already-issued admin tokens continue to work until refresh.

---

## Story Goal

Introduce a data-driven role and permission model so that administrators can:

1. View, create, and update roles.
2. View the catalogue of permissions available in the CRM.
3. Assign or remove permissions from roles.
4. Assign or remove roles for users.
5. Have authorization enforced consistently on the backend based on the user's effective permissions (the union of permissions across their assigned roles).

The initial seeded roles are **Administrator**, **Manager**, **Agent**, and **Customer**. The seeded administrator user must continue to work with no manual intervention after migration. Frontend visibility of admin-only actions must be driven by permissions returned from the API, not by hard-coded role names.

**Not in scope:** row-level / data-scoped authorization (branch or department), permission inheritance between roles, approval workflows, password reset, and any of the modules listed under "Out of scope" in the intake.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** authorization is binary — `User.IsAdmin == true` grants everything; any other authenticated user is a "plain user". Admin-only endpoints check `IsAdmin` directly.
- **New behaviour:** authorization is permission-based. A user has zero or more roles; each role has zero or more permissions; effective permissions = union across the user's roles. Endpoints declare the permission they require. The seeded administrator user is assigned the seeded Administrator role, which is granted every permission in the catalogue. `User.IsAdmin` remains for backward-compat during migration and is treated as "member of Administrator role" for the seeder, but new code **must not** branch on `IsAdmin` for authorization decisions.
- **Eligible-permissions filtering per role.** The Roles UI must **not** present the full permission catalogue for every role. Each of the four seeded system roles is only eligible for a fixed, documented subset of the catalogue, matching its real-world responsibility. This eligibility list is defined **once, on the backend**, as the single source of truth (`Permissions.cs` — see §2) and is served to the frontend via the API; it is not a hard-coded frontend hide. `PUT /api/roles/{id}/permissions` also rejects (400) any submitted code that falls outside a system role's eligible set, so the rule is enforced, not merely presented. Custom (non-system) roles created by an admin are not restricted by this matrix — they may hold any catalogue permission, since they have no fixed "type". See the **Eligible Permissions Matrix** below.

### Eligible Permissions Matrix

| Role | Eligible permission codes |
|---|---|
| **Administrator** | Full catalogue — every permission listed in §2 (`users.*`, `roles.*`, `permissions.*`, `departments.*`, `branches.*`, `tickets.*`, `customers.*`, `kb.*`, `reports.view`, `system.*`, `audit.view`, `portal.access`). |
| **Manager** | `users.view`, `users.update`, `customers.view`, `customers.create`, `customers.update`, `tickets.view`, `tickets.create`, `tickets.update`, `tickets.delete`, `tickets.assign`, `kb.view`, `kb.create`, `kb.update`, `reports.view`, `branches.view`, `departments.view`. |
| **Agent** | `tickets.view`, `tickets.create`, `tickets.update`, `customers.view`, `customers.update`, `kb.view`, `kb.create`, `kb.update`, `reports.view`. |
| **Customer** | `portal.access`, `tickets.view`, `tickets.create`, `tickets.update`. |

None of Manager, Agent, or Customer are ever eligible for `roles.*`, `permissions.*`, `system.*`, `audit.view`, `users.create`, `users.delete`, `branches.create`, `branches.update`, `departments.create`, or `departments.update` — those stay Administrator-only unless a future story's requirements explicitly extend this matrix. Agent is additionally never eligible for `tickets.delete` or `tickets.assign`. Customer is never eligible for anything outside `portal.access` and its own three ticket permissions. This matrix defines what a role **may** hold; the default grants seeded in §5 remain the (smaller) starting set — admins can grant more, up to the eligible set, via the UI.

### 2 — Permission catalogue (source of truth)

Create file: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Authorization/Permissions.cs`

Contains **constants** for every permission code the codebase references, grouped in nested static classes so the executor can autocomplete them:

```csharp
public static class Permissions
{
    public static class Users        { public const string View="users.view"; public const string Create="users.create"; public const string Update="users.update"; public const string Delete="users.delete"; }
    public static class Roles        { public const string View="roles.view"; public const string Create="roles.create"; public const string Update="roles.update"; }
    public static class PermissionsMgmt { public const string View="permissions.view"; public const string Assign="permissions.assign"; }
    public static class Departments  { public const string View="departments.view"; public const string Create="departments.create"; public const string Update="departments.update"; }
    public static class Branches     { public const string View="branches.view"; public const string Create="branches.create"; public const string Update="branches.update"; }
    public static class Tickets      { public const string View="tickets.view"; public const string Create="tickets.create"; public const string Update="tickets.update"; public const string Delete="tickets.delete"; public const string Assign="tickets.assign"; }
    public static class Customers    { public const string View="customers.view"; public const string Create="customers.create"; public const string Update="customers.update"; public const string Delete="customers.delete"; }
    public static class KnowledgeBase{ public const string View="kb.view"; public const string Create="kb.create"; public const string Update="kb.update"; public const string Delete="kb.delete"; }
    public static class Reports      { public const string View="reports.view"; }
    public static class SystemConfig { public const string View="system.view"; public const string Update="system.update"; }
    public static class AuditLogs    { public const string View="audit.view"; }
    public static class CustomerPortal { public const string Access="portal.access"; }

    public static IReadOnlyList<PermissionDefinition> All => _all;
    private static readonly PermissionDefinition[] _all = { /* enumerate the codes above with Category + DisplayName */ };

    /// Keyed by the system role's NormalizedName ("ADMINISTRATOR", "MANAGER", "AGENT", "CUSTOMER").
    /// This is the single source of truth for the Eligible Permissions Matrix (see Product rules) —
    /// the API and the frontend both read from it; neither hard-codes its own copy.
    public static IReadOnlyDictionary<string, IReadOnlySet<string>> EligibleBySystemRole => _eligibleBySystemRole;
    private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, IReadOnlySet<string>> _eligibleBySystemRole = new Dictionary<string, IReadOnlySet<string>>
    {
        ["ADMINISTRATOR"] = _all.Select(p => p.Code).ToHashSet(), // full catalogue
        ["MANAGER"] = new HashSet<string> { Users.View, Users.Update, Customers.View, Customers.Create, Customers.Update,
            Tickets.View, Tickets.Create, Tickets.Update, Tickets.Delete, Tickets.Assign,
            KnowledgeBase.View, KnowledgeBase.Create, KnowledgeBase.Update, Reports.View, Branches.View, Departments.View },
        ["AGENT"] = new HashSet<string> { Tickets.View, Tickets.Create, Tickets.Update, Customers.View, Customers.Update,
            KnowledgeBase.View, KnowledgeBase.Create, KnowledgeBase.Update, Reports.View },
        ["CUSTOMER"] = new HashSet<string> { CustomerPortal.Access, Tickets.View, Tickets.Create, Tickets.Update },
    };
}

public sealed record PermissionDefinition(string Code, string Category, string DisplayName, string? Description = null);
```

Register `Permissions.All` as a singleton `IPermissionCatalog` in `Program.cs` so the seeder and controllers share one source of truth. `IPermissionCatalog` gains a method `IReadOnlyList<PermissionDefinition> EligibleFor(Role role)` — returns `All` when `role.IsSystem == false` or `role.NormalizedName == "ADMINISTRATOR"`, otherwise filters `All` down to `EligibleBySystemRole[role.NormalizedName]`. Every consumer (API and UI) calls this one method rather than re-deriving eligibility.

Create file: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Authorization/PermissionAuthorizationHandler.cs`

```csharp
public sealed class PermissionAuthorizationHandler : AuthorizationHandler<PermissionRequirement>
{
    protected override Task HandleRequirementAsync(AuthorizationHandlerContext ctx, PermissionRequirement req)
    {
        if (ctx.User.HasPermission(req.Permission)) ctx.Succeed(req);
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }
}
```

### 5 — Extend `DbSeeder`

Update `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Infrastructure/Persistence/DbSeeder.cs`:

- After the existing admin user seeding block, add the following idempotent steps in one transaction / `SaveChangesAsync`:
  1. Ensure a `Permission` row exists for every entry in `IPermissionCatalog.All` (match by `Code`).
  2. Ensure the four system roles exist by `NormalizedName`: `ADMINISTRATOR`, `MANAGER`, `AGENT`, `CUSTOMER`, each with `IsSystem = true`.

Endpoints (all `[Authorize]` + `[HasPermission(...)]`):

| Method | Route | Permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/roles` | `roles.view` | List roles (id, name, description, isSystem, permission codes). |
| `GET` | `/api/roles/{id}` | `roles.view` | Single role detail. |
| `GET` | `/api/roles/{id}/eligible-permissions` | `roles.view` | Returns the catalogue subset (grouped by `Category`) this role is eligible to hold — `IPermissionCatalog.EligibleFor(role)`. Full catalogue for Administrator and for any custom (non-system) role; the matching row of the Eligible Permissions Matrix for Manager/Agent/Customer. The `RolePermissionsPage` renders exactly this list, never the raw `/api/permissions` catalogue. |
| `POST` | `/api/roles` | `roles.create` | Create custom (non-system) role; reject duplicate `NormalizedName`. |
| `PUT` | `/api/roles/{id}` | `roles.update` | Rename / update description. Forbid renaming the Administrator role. |
| `PUT` | `/api/roles/{id}/permissions` | `permissions.assign` | Replace the role's permission set with the provided list. Forbid modifying Administrator's permissions (always all). Unknown codes → 400. For a system role other than Administrator, any submitted code **not** in `IPermissionCatalog.EligibleFor(role)` → `400 Bad Request` with error code `permission_not_eligible_for_role` and the offending codes — this is the enforcement half of the Eligible Permissions Matrix, not just a UI hide. Custom roles are unrestricted. |

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty permission list on a role.** Users assigned only to that role authenticate successfully, get zero `permission` claims, and are blocked from every permission-protected endpoint with 403. Enforced by `PermissionAuthorizationHandler` (no claim → no `Succeed`).
- **Unknown permission code in `PUT /api/roles/{id}/permissions`.** Return `400 Bad Request` with the offending codes. Enforced in `RolesService` by validating against `IPermissionCatalog`.
- **Rename or delete the Administrator role.** Reject with `409 Conflict` (rename) or `405 Method Not Allowed` (delete — the story does not add a delete endpoint at all). Enforced in `RolesService`.
- **Removing the last Administrator role from the last admin.** Reject with `400 Bad Request` and error code `last_administrator`. Enforced in the `DELETE /api/users/{id}/roles/{roleId}` endpoint.
- **Duplicate role name.** Reject on create/update with `409 Conflict`. Enforced by unique index on `NormalizedName` + pre-check.
- **Concurrent role permission edits.** Last write wins; the replace-set endpoint clears and reinserts inside one transaction so partial states cannot leak.
- **Token replay after role change.** Existing tokens keep their old permissions until expiry. This matches the intake's guidance to reuse the existing token/refresh design — do not add token revocation in this story. Document this in the API summary comment on `AuthController`.
- **Seeded admin without any `UserRole` row after migration.** `DbSeeder` (Step 5) creates the missing link on every startup, so a partially applied migration self-heals on next boot.
- **User with `IsAdmin = true` but no Administrator role after failed seed.** Authorization no longer honours `IsAdmin`; the user would lose privileges. Mitigation: the seeder unconditionally re-adds the link at startup. Log a warning if `IsAdmin` and role-membership disagree.
- **Frontend loses `permissions` on refresh.** `AuthContext` calls `/api/auth/me` on mount when a token is present; if the request fails, treat the user as unauthenticated and clear the token.
- **User without any role.** Frontend hides admin nav; backend returns 403 on protected calls. Home page (`HomePage.tsx`) must still render.
- **Non-Latin role names (unicode).** Names are stored as `nvarchar(128)`; `NormalizedName` uses `ToUpperInvariant()`. Confirm no accidental collation-driven collisions in the unique index.
- **Assigning a permission outside a system role's eligible set.** e.g. `PUT /api/roles/{customerRoleId}/permissions` with `["users.view"]`. Rejected with `400 Bad Request` and error code `permission_not_eligible_for_role`, listing the offending codes. Enforced in `RolesService` via `IPermissionCatalog.EligibleFor(role)`, independent of and in addition to the frontend only rendering eligible checkboxes.
- **Renaming a system role.** `Role.Rename` only forbids renaming Administrator (line 85). Eligibility lookups key off `NormalizedName` at the time the role was seeded (`MANAGER`/`AGENT`/`CUSTOMER`), so if Manager/Agent/Customer's `Rename` is ever exposed in the UI, renaming would break the eligibility mapping. Out of scope for this story's UI (only description is editable per `RoleFormPage.tsx`), but note it here so a future story doesn't silently break the matrix — a longer-term fix would key eligibility off a stable `SystemRoleKind` field rather than `NormalizedName`.

## Migration / Rollback

- New migration `AddRolesAndPermissions` is additive (creates tables and FKs); no destructive schema changes. Rollback: `dotnet ef database update <previous>` reverts to `AddUserIsAdmin`.
- **Half-applied state:** if the migration ran but `DbSeeder` did not complete, users may authenticate with zero permissions and be locked out of admin UIs. Recovery: restart the API (seeder is idempotent and re-links the admin user to the Administrator role and grants all permissions). As a break-glass, an operator can `UPDATE Users SET IsAdmin = 1 WHERE Email = '<admin>'` and restart — the seeder will then re-establish the link.
- Do **not** drop `Users.IsAdmin` in this story. A follow-up story can remove it after every environment has migrated cleanly.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** run `dotnet build backend/CustomerSupportCrm.slnx` from repo root.
2. **Migration applies:** run `dotnet ef database update --project backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Infrastructure --startup-project backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api` and confirm the four new tables exist.
3. **Backend tests:** run `dotnet test` at the solution level.
4. **API smoke:** run `dotnet run --project backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api`, log in as the seeded admin, decode the JWT, and confirm one `permission` claim per catalogue entry.
5. **API authz smoke:** create a user via `POST /api/users`, assign only the Agent role, log in as that user, verify `GET /api/roles` returns `403 Forbidden` and `GET /api/auth/me` returns the Agent permission list.
6. **Frontend runs:** run `pnpm install && pnpm dev` from `frontend/`. Log in as admin, navigate to `/roles`, create a role, assign permissions, assign that role to a user.
7. **Frontend tests:** run `pnpm test` from `frontend/`.
8. **Regression:** log in as the seeded admin after migration; verify the Users list still loads, the "New user" button is visible, and all previously working actions still succeed. Verify a legacy `IsAdmin = 1` user (if any exists in a lower environment) is auto-linked to the Administrator role on the next API restart.

- [ ] Administrators can create and update roles via the UI (`roles.create`, `roles.update`).
- [ ] Administrators can list all permissions via the UI (`permissions.view`).
- [ ] Administrators can replace a role's permission set via the UI (`permissions.assign`).
- [ ] Administrators can assign and remove roles for a user via the user detail page.
- [ ] Login response and `/api/auth/me` expose the caller's effective permissions.
- [ ] Every previously admin-gated endpoint is now gated by `[HasPermission(...)]`; grep for `IsAdmin` in the API project returns no authorization-flow usages.
- [ ] Unauthorized calls return `403 Forbidden` (not `401` when authenticated).
- [ ] Frontend hides or disables actions the current user cannot perform.
- [ ] Opening the Permissions page for the Manager, Agent, or Customer role renders only the checkboxes in that role's row of the Eligible Permissions Matrix (no admin-only rows at all, not even disabled) — Administrator and custom roles still see the full catalogue. `PUT /api/roles/{id}/permissions` rejects any code outside a system role's eligible set with `400`/`permission_not_eligible_for_role`, so the restriction is enforced by the API, not just hidden in the UI.
- [ ] Seeded administrator continues to work end-to-end after migration.
- [ ] `Users.IsAdmin` column is preserved (not dropped) in this story.
- [ ] Backend and frontend test suites pass.
- [ ] The `AddRolesAndPermissions` migration applies cleanly on a fresh database and on an existing database at `AddUserIsAdmin`.
